title: Project changes · Practice
description: Explain how a predictive project evaluates, approves and communicates changes to its agreed plan. Three original practice questions.

keyIdeas.text: On a predictive project, record proposed changes to the agreed scope and analyse their combined effects on schedule, cost, quality and risk before committing to them.
Follow the agreed change process and decision authority before implementing a change to a controlled baseline; a request alone is not approval.
After a change is approved, update the affected baseline and working documents through the agreed process, communicate the decision and track implementation.

misconceptions: A small-sounding scope change cannot affect schedule or cost.
Any stakeholder request automatically authorises work.
A verbal approval means project records no longer need updating.
